request.spec:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.
request.prompt:

DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

agent.result_text:
I added an **Export policy versions (CSV)** button (`data-testid="export-policy"`). `bin/e2e` now passes all 4 tests.

It downloads `policy-<sheet>.csv`, with the header `version,from,key,value,claims,due-total` and then one line per policy version, in the order the versions were made:
- **version, key, value** come from the existing `/api/sheets/{id}/policy-versions` endpoint. A blank value is written as empty.
- **from** is the date the version starts: its from-date, or the sheet's today when it was made if it had no from-date.
- **claims** counts the claims that a person's due-total includes (the same set the totals use), and puts each one under the version in force on the claim's date.
- **due-total** adds up those claims' dues, as the claim rows show them.

All the work happens in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/features/export/export.slot.tsx`, next to the other CSV exports and built the same way. I didn't need to change the server or the stored data, and the export writes nothing to the audit file.

The request didn't say exactly which claims count. I took "count" to mean the claims included in the due-totals, so draft and void claims are left out, and so are deferred ones. The test agrees with this reading: a claim dated before the first version is left out because no version was in force on its date, and putting a person on hold doesn't change their claims' count.

probe.probe_text:
I read the code without changing anything. The domain logic lives mainly in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/{claim,person,rollup,period,setting}` and is reimplemented in the front end in `src/main/frontend/features/{rates,claims,overdue,periods,header,…}`. When a comment and the code disagree, I describe what the **code** does and note the conflict.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Per claim (claim row, `claims.slot.tsx` ~l.296–323)
- **Status (`ClaimStatus`)**: DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED, VOID, DELETED, REVIEW. The allowed moves are in the switch in `ApplyClaimStatus.applyJudged`:
  - OPEN only from DRAFT; SETTLE only from OPEN; APPROVE/REJECT only from PENDING.
  - VOID from any status except DELETED; RESETTLE only from SETTLED.
  - DELETE only from DRAFT; RESTORE only from DELETED; REVIEW only from REVIEW.
- **Number (`ClaimNumbering.next`)**: assigned in `SaveClaimStatus` when a claim becomes SETTLED (settle or approve), not when it is opened. The comments in `Claim.java`, `claims.ts` and `ApplyClaimStatus` all say "when opened"; the code disagrees.
  - The format is `FY<yyyy>-<n>`, counted by the fiscal year of the due-by (setting `fiscal-start-month`) and shared across the sheet's tree.
  - While `period-numbering-from` is on or before today, the format is `<period>-<n>`, or `X-<n>` when no period contains the due-by.
  - A voided claim keeps its number.
- **Due (`claim-due`)**:
  - Server: `ClaimDue.figure` then `LateCharge.add`. Client: `rates.ts claimDue`.
  - Order of precedence:
    1. The frozen `due`, if settled.
    2. Otherwise `statedDue`, if `bound` (`stated`).
    3. Otherwise the live figure `ClaimDue.live`: amount × the grade's rate / 100.
  - The live figure uses the grade the person had on the claim's date (`gradeOn`). The rate is looked up with `RateRepository.forClaim` and `rates.seqOf`: a forward-only rate saved after the claim was added does not apply to it. If the sheet has no rate, the parent sheets are searched up to `PARENT_LEVELS` = 3. No rate at all gives **n/a**.
  - **Floor**: the result is at least `floor` (default 1.00, in force on the claim's date). Corrections and settled figures are not floored.
  - **Late charge (`LateCharge.on`)**: added after the floor.
- **Rounding (`Rounding.mode`)**: two decimals.
  - A dated `rounding` setting (half-up or half-even) in force on `roundsOn` decides.
  - Otherwise: half-up before `policy-date`, half-even on or after it. When `policy-date` is blank, the sheet's today stands in.
  - `roundsOn` is the corrected claim's date for a correction, otherwise the claim's own date.
- **Late charge (`LateCharge.on`)**:
  - Applies only to OPEN/PENDING claims that are not settled, not a correction, not `deferred` and not `waived`.
  - `lateFrom` = `dueBy` + `grace-<grade>`.
  - For each full 30 days (`DAYS`) past `lateFrom`, it adds the `late-pct` in force on that boundary date, applied to figure + earlier charges (it compounds), rounding each step.
  - A bound claim keeps its stated figure. Settling freezes the charge into the due.
- **Due-by (`claim-due-by`, `ClaimRules.dueBy`/`terms`)**:
  - The terms-th business day after the claim's date. `HolidayRepository.businessDaysAfter` skips weekends and holidays.
  - The terms come from the person's own `termsOn(today)`, else `terms-<grade>`, else `terms` (default 14). All are taken **on the day the claim is added**, not on the claim's date.
  - The due-by is fixed when the claim is added, and recalculated when a holiday is added (`refixDueBys`). A steward can set it directly (`ApplyDueBy`).
- **Overdue (`claim-overdue`, `late.ts isOverdue`)**: the claim is open, not deferred, and `lateFrom` < today.
- **Period (`claim-period`)**: the period containing the **due-by**, not the claim's date.
- **Flags**:
  - `stated` (`bound`): set when the person's last statement bound the claim.
  - `deferred` (`ClaimDue.deferred`): the claim counts, is not bound, and `deferredUntil` > today. On screen, a VOID claim with a future `deferredUntil` also shows "yes".
  - `held` (`ApplyClaimHold`): only OPEN or PENDING claims can be held.
  - `waived`, `lateEntry` (added while the period was soft-closed), `review-late` and `pending-late` (`isReviewLate`/`isPendingLate`, using the `review-sla`/`pending-sla` days counted from the latest REVIEW/PENDING log line), plus `proofs`, `corrects` and `splitFrom`.
- **Corrections (`Corrections.check`)**: a negative amount must name a SETTLED claim of the same person. It cannot exceed what remains of that claim (its amount less the non-void, non-deleted corrections already made against it).

### Which claims count (`ClaimDue`, client `claims.ts live`/`counts`)
- `counts`: OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED.
- `countsLive` / `countsClaimed` (they are identical): `counts`, and not `deferred`, and not `retiredOut`.
- `retiredOut`: the claim is open, not bound, and the person's retirement date is on or before today.
- **Holds do not remove a claim from the totals.** `countsLive(claim, person)` ignores holds. This contradicts the comments in `Claim.java`, `Person.java` and `ApplyClaimHold`, which say held claims "count in no live total". The comments in `ClaimDue` and `claims.ts` agree with the code.
  - A person's hold only gives them a 0.00 pool cut on days it covers (`PoolRepository.cuts`).

### Per person (person row)
- **`person-claimed`**: the amounts of counting claims added up, leaving out corrections. Client: `claimed(liveClaimed(...))`.
- **`person-due-total`** (`Rollup.take`, client `rates.ts personDue`):
  1. Add up the live figures.
  2. Adjust for share parts (`shareParts`): a holder gains `amount × share × their own grade's rate`, or `due × share` once settled; the claim's owner loses the same amount.
  3. Cap it (`SettingRepository.capped`): at most `cap` − cut total, not below 0.00. The cap used is the one in force on the date of the person's latest counting claim, or today if none counts.
  - Shows **n/a** when the grade has no rate today and nothing has a figure.
- **`person-excess`**: the amount the cap removed.
- **`person-settled-total` / `person-open-total`** (`personSplit`): the same figures split by SETTLED versus OPEN/PENDING.
- **`person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`**: totals over overdue claims; not capped.
- **`person-score`** (`score`): settled figures (corrections excluded) / 100, minus 5 per overdue claim, rounded half-even to a whole number.
- **`person-band`**: HIGH or MID or LOW against `score-high`/`score-mid`; blank if either threshold is blank.
- **`person-active`** (`isActive`): has an open counting claim dated in the last 30 days.
- **`person-aged-0-30/31-60/61`**: dues of open claims bucketed by the claim date's age.
- **`person-claims-OPEN/SETTLED-count`**: counts by raw status.
- **`person-cut-total`**: from pools.
- **`person-stated-total`**: from the last statement.
- **Per-period figures**:
  - `person-period-*-due-total` (`personPeriodDue`): claims whose due-by is in the period, judged by their status at the period's end (`statusAsOf`).
  - `person-period-*-carried`: claims from earlier periods that were still open at the period's end, plus pasted openings.
- **Grade and terms**: dated (`gradeOn`, `termsOn`). The grade shown is the one in force today.

### Sheet totals (`Rollup`, client `header/totals.ts`)
- `claimed-total`: a plain sum.
- `due-total` and `overdue-total` (`trimmedTotal`/`trimmedSum`): skip n/a, then drop the single highest and lowest value when 3 or more remain.
- The audit file gets ROLLUP, TOTALS and ALERT lines. ALERT is written when a person's due-total crosses `alert-threshold`.
- The summary also shows grade due (retired people excluded), period due and its change, and counts by status and by void reason.

### Who may do what (`ApplyClaimStatus`, `SettingRepository.PERMISSIONS`)
- **Roles**: `RoleRepository.roleOf` gives clerk by default; a user is a steward while a delegation to them is active.
- **Permissions** (`perm-*` settings): default open/settle/void/close = clerk or steward; reassign/reopen = steward; changing today = clerk, steward or restricted.
- **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim, or last edited it, cannot settle or approve it.
- **Clerk limit**: a clerk settling a claim whose due is above `clerk-limit` (or the grade's own limit) sends it to PENDING instead. Only a steward or the person's approver can approve or reject it.
- **Thresholds**:
  - Above `proof-threshold` (plus any `proof-kinds`): settle and approve are refused without proof.
  - Above `note-threshold`: opening needs a note.
  - Above `review-threshold`: opening sends the claim to REVIEW, and only a steward can review it.
- **Caps on open claims**: the period `cap` (`overCap`) and `max-open` (`overMaxOpen`) block opening.
- **Flag**: while a flag is in force (until its until-date, inclusive), only a steward can open the person's claims.
- **Steward-only**:
  - Voiding a SETTLED claim, and only within 7 days of settling (`VOID_SETTLED_DAYS`).
  - Re-settling, which refixes the due at today's figure.
  - Locking a period.
- **Void reasons**: required while the sheet has a list of them.
- **Deleted drafts**: can only be restored on the same sheet-today they were deleted.
- **Deferred claims**: cannot be settled.
- **Settle as of a date** (`ClaimDueAsOf`): the date must be on or before today; the due is the one as of that date.

### Dates, editing, periods, imports
- **Claim date**: defaults to the `entry-date` setting, else today.
  - It must not be after the retirement date, nor inside a past retirement (`mayClaimOn`).
  - The claim's `ref` must be unique on the sheet, ignoring case.
  - Only a DRAFT can be edited (`ApplyClaim`).
- **Closed period** (`closedOn`, judged by due-by): refuses adds, edits and every status change.
  - Closing (`PeriodCloser.close`) freezes `closedTotal`, `personTotals`, `personCarried` and pool cuts.
  - **Soft-close** freezes the same figures but still allows changes.
  - **Reopen** needs `perm-reopen` and is refused while the period is locked.
  - **`AutoClosePeriods`**: changing today closes every open period whose to-date + `grace-days` is before the new today.
- **Import** (`CheckImportedPeople`/`AddImportedPeople`): all or nothing.
  - A line matching a name or alias edits that person: the grade is taken from today; terms and contact only if the line gives them.
  - Other lines add a person.
  - A person matched twice refuses the whole import.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It is not in one place, so a new developer would find it hard to pick up. The rules are spread over hundreds of one-method Java classes and long comments. The whole figure engine is also written a second time in TypeScript (`rates.ts`, `claims.ts`, `late.ts`, `periods.ts`), and the copies drift: the client's `counts` excludes deferred claims but the server's doesn't. Comments also contradict the code on whether holds remove claims from totals and on when claims get their number, so the comments can't be trusted without reading the code.
